etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English grape, from Old French grape, grappe, crape (“cluster of fruit or flowers, bunch of grapes”), from graper, craper (“to pick grapes”, literally “to hook”), of Germanic origin, from Frankish *krappō (“hook”), from Proto-Indo-European *greb- (“hook”), *gremb- (“crooked, uneven”), from *ger- (“to turn, bend, twist”). Cognate with Middle Dutch krappe (“hook”), Old High German krapfo (“hook”) (whence German Krapfen (“Berliner doughnut”). Doublet of grappa. More at cramp.

definitions.definition: (countable) A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on vines of genus Vitis.
(countable, uncountable) A woody vine of genus Vitis that bears clusters of grapes; a grapevine.
(countable) Any of various fruits or plants with varying resemblances to those of genus Vitis but belonging to other genera; their edibility varies.
(countable, uncountable) A dark purplish-red colour, the colour of many grapes.
(pathology) A mangy tumour on a horse's leg.
(US, naval slang) A purple-shirted technician responsible for refueling aircraft.

quote.text: I was horrified to see three grapes standing by the aircraft with the hose still connected.

definitions.definition: (US, slang, colloquial, African-American Vernacular) A person's head.
Containing grapes or having a grape flavor.
Of a dark purplish red colour.

quote.citation: 1973, Nancy Safford, Time's Island; Portraits of the Vineyard, page 35:
quote.text: I used to go graping and blackberrying and blueberrying.

definitions.definition: (of livestock) To develop tubercules as a result of tuberculosis.

quote.citation: 1856, Great Britain Parliament House of Commons, Reports from Committees, page 138:
quote.text: Some are called ticked; some have the milk fever; some have worm-'ith-tail ; some are graped ; others are broken-up old cows.
The lungs were in a bad condition, hard in places, and lumpy and badly graped.

quote.citation: 1898, Great Britain Royal Commission on Tuberculosis, Report of the Royal Commission Appointed to Inquire Into the Administrative Procedures for Controlling Danger to Man Through the Use as Food of the Meat and Milk of Tuberculous Animals, page 245:
quote.text: Do I understand that the carcases of the graped cows, to which you refer, were used for food ?

definitions.definition: To develop a texture with small grape-like clusters of a contaminant or foreign substance.

quote.text: Over the huge abraded rind, Crow-countries graped with dung, we go, Past gullies that no longer flow And wells that nobody can find, Lashed by the screaming of the crow, Stabbed by the needles of the mind.

quote.citation: 1991, Desheng Li, Tectonic types of oil and gas basins in China, page 162:
quote.text: Some small graped pisolitic textures are primary but not important.

quote.citation: 2012, K. Subramanian, Lead-free Solders: Materials Reliability for Electronics, →ISBN, page 169:
quote.text: An additional concern is the problem of graping, which becomes more visible when type-4 solder powder is required for fine-pitch μ-BGA attachment.

quote.text: Aw graped my way out i' the dark, An' down the stairs aw scrafflel'd

I dinna ken,” said Steenie ; “ the book had fa'en out 0' his pocket, I fancy, for I fand it amang my feet when I was graping about to set him on his legs again, and I just pat it in my pouch to keep it safe ;
